name: S3
scope: A person with INTERMEDIATE proficiency level in S3 as a competency should be able to design and manage S3 buckets and object structures for business domains, implement efficient key naming and partitioning strategies, configure IAM policies, bucket policies, and S3 Block Public Access for secure access control, and use server-side encryption (SSE-S3, SSE-KMS) and object versioning for data protection. They should understand S3 storage classes (Standard, IA, Intelligent-Tiering, Glacier), lifecycle policies for cost optimization, and replication (SRR, CRR) for durability and DR. They can integrate S3 with AWS compute (EC2, Lambda, ECS/EKS), analytics (Athena, Glue, EMR), and event-driven workflows (SNS, SQS, Lambda notifications), and use pre-signed URLs and CORS for web/mobile access. They monitor S3 using CloudWatch, Storage Lens, CloudTrail, and server access logs, troubleshoot common issues (403, 404, CORS, permissions), and automate operations via CLI, SDK, CloudFormation/CDK, and CI/CD pipelines. They can plan and execute migrations using CLI, DataSync, Snowball, and Storage Gateway, validate data integrity, and manage hybrid/on-prem connectivity. They document S3 designs, lifecycle, and security, collaborate with security/compliance teams, and onboard juniors to best practices, tagging, and operational runbooks.

{"sections":[{"name":"Core S3 Concepts & Architecture","scope_included":"- Understands S3’s role as object storage (not block or file) and chooses it appropriately for workloads like static content, logs, data lakes, backups, and archives
- Knows key S3 characteristics and guarantees:
  - Regional service with data replicated across multiple AZs within a Region
  - 11 9s durability and typical availability targets per storage class
  - Strong read-after-write consistency for PUTs of new objects and overwrite/delete behavior
- Understands S3 resource model and addressing:
  - Global uniqueness of bucket names and Region scoping of buckets
  - Object keys, prefixes, and folder-like behavior as key naming conventions
  - Virtual-hosted–style vs path-style URLs and current AWS recommendations
- Can explain S3 request and operation types:
  - PUT, GET, DELETE, COPY, LIST, HEAD, multipart upload, and range requests
  - Difference between object data, system metadata, and user-defined metadata
- Understands basic limits and quotas relevant at this level:
  - Practically unlimited storage and object count per bucket
  - Request rate scaling characteristics and how prefix distribution affects it
- Knows when S3 is appropriate vs EFS, EBS, FSx, or on-prem storage in typical solution designs","is_non_core_section":false},{"name":"Bucket, Object Design & Data Modeling","scope_included":"- Designs bucket structures aligned with business domains, environments, and lifecycle needs rather than ad hoc, per-application buckets
- Uses object key naming schemes that support:
  - Efficient listing and partitioning (time-based, customer-based, region-based patterns)
  - Performance and parallelism for high request rates
  - Easier lifecycle management and governance
- Understands and uses object metadata effectively:
  - System metadata (Content-Type, Content-Encoding, Cache-Control, etc.)
  - Custom metadata and object tags for classification, lifecycle, and access control
- Knows how to organize data lakes or analytics datasets on S3:
  - Partitioning strategy (by date, region, tenant, etc.)
  - Naming conventions suitable for Athena/Glue/EMR/Spark
- Capable of planning multi-bucket strategies:
  - Separation by environment (dev/test/stage/prod)
  - Separation by security boundary or regulatory requirement
  - Separation by workload (logs, raw data, curated data, backups)
- Understands trade-offs between fewer, larger buckets vs more, smaller buckets in terms of manageability, policy complexity, and isolation","is_non_core_section":false},{"name":"Security, Access Control & Compliance","scope_included":"- Applies least-privilege access using AWS IAM and S3-native controls:
  - IAM user/role policies granting scoped S3 actions on specific buckets/prefixes
  - Bucket policies for cross-account and public access control
  - Awareness of legacy ACLs and how to avoid or minimize their use
- Configures and interprets S3 Block Public Access settings at account and bucket levels
- Manages Object Ownership settings (Bucket owner enforced vs object writer) and understands impact on ACLs and cross-account uploads
- Designs and troubleshoots access scenarios:
  - Cross-account access using IAM roles and bucket policies
  - Service access (CloudFront, Lambda, ECS/EKS tasks, Glue, EMR, etc.) via IAM roles
  - Public content hosting while keeping sensitive data private
- Implements encryption strategies:
  - Server-side encryption with SSE-S3 and SSE-KMS, default bucket encryption
  - Client-side encryption basics and when it is needed
  - KMS key policies, key rotation, and performance/cost considerations
- Uses S3 Access Points and, where appropriate, VPC-only access points to simplify and secure access for multiple applications or accounts
- Configures and uses VPC gateway endpoints for S3:
  - Ensures private access from VPCs without traversing the public internet
  - Uses endpoint policies to further restrict access
- Understands compliance-related features and their operational use:
  - S3 Object Lock (governance vs compliance mode), retention periods, legal holds
  - Data residency considerations (Region choice, replication destinations)
- Regularly audits S3 security posture:
  - Uses tools like IAM Access Analyzer, S3 console public access checks, and S3 Storage Lens security metrics
  - Reviews CloudTrail logs for sensitive operations (e.g., PutBucketPolicy, DeleteBucketEncryption)","is_non_core_section":false},{"name":"Performance, Scalability & Cost Optimization","scope_included":"- Understands how S3 scales for throughput and request rates and how to design for it:
  - Key naming patterns that support high concurrency
  - Use of multipart uploads for large objects and parallelism
- Uses range GETs and multipart uploads for large media, backups, or big data objects when appropriate
- Knows S3 storage classes and can choose and justify them:
  - Standard, Standard-IA, One Zone-IA
  - Intelligent-Tiering and its tiers, monitoring overhead, and use cases
  - Glacier Instant Retrieval, Glacier Flexible Retrieval, Glacier Deep Archive
- Designs lifecycle and storage class strategies for cost efficiency while maintaining performance and access needs
- Understands cost dimensions for S3:
  - Storage costs across classes
  - Request and data retrieval costs
  - Data transfer (inter-AZ, inter-Region, internet egress, CloudFront vs S3 direct)
  - Replication and replication time control costs
- Uses features and tools to manage and reduce costs:
  - S3 Storage Lens and AWS Cost Explorer for usage and cost patterns
  - Lifecycle transitions and expirations to manage cold data and delete obsolete data
  - Intelligent-Tiering for unpredictable access patterns
- Designs around performance pitfalls:
  - Minimizing unnecessary LIST/GET operations
  - Avoiding inefficient small-object patterns when inappropriate
  - Understanding and mitigating 503 Slow Down or throttling behaviors","is_non_core_section":false},{"name":"Data Protection, Durability & Availability","scope_included":"- Configures and uses versioning to protect against accidental deletes and overwrites:
  - Interprets current vs non-current versions and delete markers
  - Works with versioned buckets via CLI/SDK/console, including restoring previous versions
- Understands and configures replication:
  - Same-Region Replication (SRR) for compliance, isolation, or logical separation
  - Cross-Region Replication (CRR) for DR and latency use cases
  - Handles replication of existing vs new objects, delete markers, and metadata
  - Awareness of Replication Time Control and when it is needed
- Applies data durability and availability patterns:
  - Uses One Zone-IA only for recreatable data and non-critical workloads
  - Uses multi-Region strategies (backup or replication) for regional outage resilience
- Understands backup and restore strategies involving S3:
  - Application-level backups to S3
  - Integration with AWS Backup, RDS, EBS snapshots, and other services that store backups in S3
- Uses S3 Object Lock with versioning as part of WORM and ransomware-resistant backup strategies for appropriate workloads
- Considers and plans for recovery time and recovery point objectives (RTO/RPO) using S3 features, replication, and lifecycle policies","is_non_core_section":false},{"name":"Data Lifecycle Management & Storage Governance","scope_included":"- Designs and manages lifecycle policies:
  - Transitioning data between storage classes based on age or last access
  - Expiring objects, non-current versions, and delete markers
  - Using filters such as prefix and object tags
- Uses object tags for lifecycle segmentation, billing, and governance across tenants or datasets
- Balances lifecycle transitions with cost and performance impact, avoiding overly aggressive transitions that increase retrieval or rehydration costs
- Manages retention and deletion policies to align with legal, regulatory, and business requirements:
  - Retention periods for logs, analytics data, documents, and backups
  - Coordinating S3 lifecycle with application-level deletion and compliance policies
- Applies governance for multi-tenant or multi-team environments:
  - Tagging for chargeback/showback
  - Clear ownership of buckets and prefixes
  - Guardrails on who can create lifecycle rules and bucket policies","is_non_core_section":false},{"name":"Application Integration & Data Processing","scope_included":"- Integrates S3 with compute and edge services:
  - EC2, ECS/EKS, Lambda, and on-prem applications using AWS SDKs
  - CloudFront for content delivery, origin access (OAC/OAI), and caching
- Uses S3 events and notifications to build event-driven architectures:
  - Configures notifications for object creation, deletion, and replication events
  - Sends notifications to SNS, SQS, and Lambda and understands delivery semantics
- Uses S3 in analytics and data lake patterns:
  - Integration with Glue (crawlers, data catalog), Athena (querying data), and EMR/Spark workloads
  - Partitioned data layout for efficient querying and cost control
- Understands use of pre-signed URLs for temporary access:
  - Generating pre-signed URLs for uploads and downloads
  - Controlling expiration and scope
- Designs upload and download flows for web and mobile applications:
  - Browser-based direct uploads to S3 (bypassing backend servers)
  - Handling CORS configuration on buckets
  - Handling large file uploads via multipart and client resumability patterns
- Familiar with S3 Object Lambda at least conceptually and can recognize when it might be appropriate to transform data on access, even if not yet deeply experienced using it","is_non_core_section":false},{"name":"Operations, Monitoring & Troubleshooting","scope_included":"- Uses AWS-native monitoring for S3:
  - CloudWatch metrics for requests, errors, and data transfer
  - S3 Storage Lens for usage trends and performance/cost/security insights
  - CloudTrail data events for object-level access auditing
- Configures and uses logging:
  - S3 server access logging
  - CloudFront logs when S3 is behind CloudFront
- Troubleshoots common S3 issues:
  - 403 and AccessDenied due to IAM, bucket policy, ACLs, or Block Public Access
  - 404 and NoSuchKey vs eventual consistency misunderstandings
  - CORS problems with browser-based access
  - Permission issues when using cross-account roles or Access Points
- Operates lifecycle, replication, and encryption at scale:
  - Safely updates bucket policies and lifecycle rules using change management
  - Validates encryption status and enforces default encryption
  - Monitors replication metrics and handles backlog conditions
- Uses S3 Batch Operations for large-scale object changes:
  - Tagging, ACL/policy changes, encryption updates, or invoking Lambda on many objects
- Demonstrates incident response skills involving S3:
  - Identifies scope of accidental deletions using versioning
  - Performs recovery using previous versions, backups, or replicated copies
  - Assesses potential data exposure in case of misconfiguration and works with security/compliance teams","is_non_core_section":false},{"name":"Migration, Data Transfer & Hybrid Connectivity","scope_included":"- Understands and uses data transfer options to and from S3:
  - AWS CLI and SDK-based transfers for moderate data volumes
  - S3 Transfer Acceleration for global uploads with high latency
  - S3 multipart uploads and resume capabilities
- Plans and executes larger migrations or bulk transfers:
  - Uses AWS DataSync for on-prem to S3 or inter-Region transfers
  - Familiarity with AWS Snowball/Snowcone for very large offline migrations
  - Uses S3 Batch Operations to modify or validate large datasets after migration
- Designs hybrid and multi-environment data flows:
  - Integration with AWS Storage Gateway for on-prem file or tape backup to S3
  - Access patterns from on-prem via VPN/Direct Connect and performance implications
- Considers cutover strategies and validation:
  - Validates data completeness and integrity post-migration (checksums, counts, sampling)
  - Plans incremental syncs and final cutover to minimize downtime and data loss
- Evaluates trade-offs between single large objects vs many small objects for migration, backup, and restore operations","is_non_core_section":false},{"name":"Tooling, Automation & Environment Setup","scope_included":"- Uses AWS Console effectively for exploration, configuration, and diagnostics while preferring automation for repeatable changes
- Proficient with AWS CLI for S3:
  - Listing, syncing, copying, moving, and deleting objects and prefixes
  - Configuring CLI profiles, regions, and credentials securely
  - Using features like `--exclude`/`--include`, `sync`, and `cp` options for efficient operations
- Uses infrastructure-as-code tools to manage S3:
  - CloudFormation or AWS CDK to define buckets, policies, lifecycle rules, encryption, and events
  - Optionally Terraform or similar tools in multi-cloud or standardized environments
- Automates common operational tasks:
  - Scheduled cleanup of temporary buckets
  - Automated application deployment artifacts to S3 (e.g., static site builds, assets)
  - Automated application logs and backups to S3
- Integrates S3 with CI/CD pipelines and build systems where relevant
- Manages credentials and access for automation and tooling securely:
  - Uses IAM roles, instance profiles, task roles instead of long-lived access keys
  - Uses least-privilege policies in automation tools and pipelines","is_non_core_section":true},{"name":"Collaboration, Governance & Documentation","scope_included":"- Documents S3-related designs clearly:
  - Bucket naming conventions and purpose
  - Lifecycle rules, retention policies, and storage class usage
  - Security model (IAM roles, bucket policies, encryption choices)
- Communicates constraints and trade-offs with stakeholders:
  - Explains cost vs performance vs durability decisions
  - Highlights impact of retention and deletion policies on legal/compliance needs
- Collaborates with security, compliance, and data teams:
  - Aligns S3 configurations with organizational security standards
  - Participates in reviews of public-facing buckets and data exposure risk
- Participates in operational runbooks and incident processes:
  - Defines standard procedures for recovery from accidental deletes or misconfigurations
  - Contributes troubleshooting steps for frequent S3 issues (access, performance, costs)
- Helps onboard junior engineers to S3 best practices:
  - Reviews their S3 usage, policies, and lifecycle rules
  - Provides guidance on secure and cost-effective patterns
- Maintains tagging and documentation standards to support cost allocation, auditing, and operational ownership","is_non_core_section":true}]}
